title: Adapter Registry
description: Every tool the orchestrator may invoke, and exactly how (backlog E1-007). 02-container-component.md requires the registry to map a fixed adapter ID to an immutable container digest and a typed command, and to declare the passive/active classification. 04-orchestrator-spec.md adds a fixed entrypoint, a typed argument array and no user input through a shell. All of that is shape here rather than policy: an adapter that wanted a shell string, an unpinned image or a destructive classification has no way to be written down.

adapter_id.description: Fixed and namespaced. A run names an adapter by this and never by a path or a command, so there is nothing to substitute.

kind.description: A container adapter runs a pinned image. A synthetic one runs in process and reaches no network at all, which is what makes it usable before any image digest is pinned.

image_ref.description: Identifier of a version-manifest image entry. Images are never written here, so an adapter cannot pin an unreviewed one. Required for a container adapter and forbidden for a synthetic one, which the tests enforce because JSON Schema alone cannot say it here.

profile.description: The same two values the scope record and the grant allow. Destructive tooling has no representation in any of the three.

entrypoint.description: One executable, no arguments and no shell metacharacters. A space here would be the beginning of a command line.

arguments.description: A typed vector, never a string. There is no representation for a command line, so there is nothing for a shell to re-parse.

artifacts.description: What this adapter can produce. An adapter that declares no artifact produces nothing anyone can ingest.

kind.description: A literal is fixed at registration. The other three are filled by the orchestrator from the pinned target, the output volume and the approved budgets. There is no free-text kind, so an operator cannot supply an argument at all.

value.description: No whitespace and no shell metacharacter. The argument vector is passed without a shell, so these could not be interpreted; refusing them anyway means a registry entry cannot be misread by a human either.
